name: combine
description: Early Haskell-Parsec-inspired combinator library; mature but slower-moving

license.comment: Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT"; GitHub reports spdx MIT. Single license.

approach.comment: Parsec-inspired parser combinator library; parsers are Rust values composed with methods/functions (map, with, skip, or, many, sep_by, chainl1...).

implementation.comment: Only required dependency is memchr (default-features off); optional deps (regex, tokio, futures, bytes, pin-project-lite) are all pure Rust.

documentation.comment: docs.rs is the primary reference; the GitHub wiki holds a quickstart tutorial (written for combine 3) plus 'Error Handling', 'Input Machinery' and 'Parser Trait' explainers.

first-release.comment: crates.io crate created 2015-07-17; GitHub repository created 2015-01-12.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 4.6.8 published 2026-08-25 (bugfix release after 4.6.7 in 2024-04). All research reflects combine 4.6.x.

grammar-class.comment: Combinator library; per Assessment Guidelines tagged 'arbitrary'. The crate docs describe its default behaviour as LL(1) with opt-in LL(k) via attempt, but no formal grammar class is enforced.

grammar-definition.comment: Parsers are Rust expressions; the macro_rules parser! macro only helps with recursive parsers / opaque types, it is not a grammar DSL.

left-recursion.comment: No left-recursion support in combine itself; chainl1/chainr1 handle left/right-associative operator chains but are not a precedence/Pratt facility. The separate combine-language crate (same author, 4.0.0 released 2026-09-18) adds expression_parser with Assoc/Fixity.

ambiguity-handling.comment: or/choice try alternatives in order; an alternative is only tried if the previous one failed without consuming input (Parsec semantics), so full backtracking needs attempt().

backtracking.comment: Inverse of a cut: parsers commit as soon as they consume input (LL(1) by default); attempt() opts into backtracking after consumption. Equivalent effect to a bounded/cut model.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over &str/&[u8]; also parses any &[T] slice (SliceStream) or any Iterator via IteratorStream, so an external lexer's tokens can be fed directly.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: Only chainl1/chainr1 in the main crate. The separate combine-language crate offers expression_parser with Assoc/Fixity tables; not counted as it is a distinct crate/repository.

unicode-aware.comment: For &str streams Token = char and ranges are &str slices; the parser::char module provides char-level primitives (letter, digit, space, string, ...). Byte-level parsing via parser::byte.

input-types.comment: &str, &[u8]/&[T], SliceStream<T>, IteratorStream, std::io::Read via stream::read / buf_reader, and user types implementing StreamOnce/Stream. No rope/text-buffer input.

streaming-partial-input.comment: PartialStream signals 'need more input' at end of stream and parsing can be resumed without losing progress; stream::decoder and tokio/futures features build on this.

zero-copy.comment: RangeStream/RangeStreamOnce return borrowed slices of the input (take_while, range, recognize).

span-tracking.comment: Default &str/&[u8] positions are PointerOffset (translatable to a byte index). Opt-in wrappers: position::Stream with IndexPositioner (byte index) or SourcePosition (line/column); the Positioner trait is user-implementable. span::Stream reports positions as Span{start,end} but the built-in impl yields zero-width spans.

output-model.comment: Parser::Output is an arbitrary user type built via map/and_then/then.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: User composes spaces()/skip_many(space()) explicitly; no implicit skip rules. combine-language's LanguageEnv adds lexeme-style whitespace/comment skipping as a separate crate.

stateful-parsing.comment: stream::state::Stream pairs a stream with user-defined state that parsers can read and mutate.

error-recovery.comment: No recovery/sync API; a parse stops at the first committed error.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: easy::Errors holds several Error entries but all at a single position (merged expected/unexpected/message info); only one failure site per run.

expected-token-reporting.comment: easy::Error::Expected entries collect what the LL(1) parser would have accepted; ParseError::set_expected is part of the error trait.

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is the stream's associated StreamOnce::Error, constrained by the ParseError trait; users implement ParseError/StreamError for their own types. Built-ins: easy::Errors, StringStreamError, UnexpectedParse.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Errors carry a single position (byte offset or line/column via position::Stream). span::Stream wraps positions in Span{start,end} but the built-in conversion produces zero-width spans; no labelled secondary spans.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No first-party or documented bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets; easy::Errors implements Display for plain-text output.

contextual-error-messages.comment: Parser::expected(msg) replaces the expected set with a label; Parser::message(msg) appends a message to the error.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Partial/resumable parsing is for streaming input, not for reusing a previous tree after an edit.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Output is whatever the user builds; no CST facility.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: README's user list contains no editor or language server; no verified usage in rust-analyzer, Helix, Zed or Neovim.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, checked 2026-09-19): combine 53 ms vs 18 ms for the hand-optimised serde_json baseline (~2.9x, upper edge of the 1.5-3x bracket); winnow 27, peg 29, chumsky 47, pest 62, nom 68. Caveat: the suite still pins combine v3.8.1, not 4.x; benchmark is maintained by winnow's author.

compile-time-impact.comment: Same benchmark: 4 s clean debug build for the combine (v3.8.1) JSON parser vs 1 s winnow, 3 s nom, 5 s chumsky, 12 s lalrpop. Deeply nested generic parser types; no proc-macros. Incremental delta not separately measured.

allocation-strategy.comment: Zero-copy ranges; core builds with --no-default-features (no std, no alloc) in CI. Collecting combinators (many, sep_by) extend a user-chosen container, which may be non-allocating.

no-std-support.comment: #![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]; features std (default) and alloc. CI runs cargo check --no-default-features. easy errors, decoder and Read streams need std; position tracking works in no_std.

msrv.comment: No rust-version field in Cargo.toml; 1.85.0 is the pinned toolchain in the CI matrix (cargo check with and without default features).

unsafe-usage.comment: No forbid(unsafe_code). src/stream/mod.rs has three unsafe blocks (bounds-checked get_unchecked in slice_uncons_while*, repr(transparent) pointer cast in CompleteStream::from); lib.rs has none. Other modules not exhaustively audited.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: No proc-macro dependencies (no syn/quote); parser!, choice!, dispatch! are macro_rules macros.

dependency-count.comment: One required dependency (memchr). Optional feature-gated deps: regex, pin-project-lite, tokio (0.2/0.3/1), tokio-util, futures-core, futures-io, bytes (0.5/1).

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: no_std-capable pure Rust with a single pure-Rust dependency and no platform-specific code; no wasm target in CI.

async-friendly.comment: First-party async support: tokio/futures-03 features, stream::decoder for async I/O, tokio-util codec integration, examples/async.rs. Parsers are plain generic values (Send when captures are).

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads, checked 2026-09-19 (~24.7M/month per lib.rs; large share via redis-rs).

maintenance-status.comment: Bugfix-only releases: 4.6.8 (2026-08-25) after 4.6.7 (2024-04) and 4.6.6 (2022-08); repo pushed 2026-09-18 merging small community PRs. No feature work since the 4.x line; 4.6.8 landed within 6 months but fits the 'responds to bugs, no features in 12+ months' definition. Not superseded, though winnow/chumsky/nom now dominate the combinator space.

documentation-quality.comment: Crate-level docs with worked examples (integer lists, recursive expressions, error output) and a stream/error/parser module overview, but docs.rs reports only ~47% of items documented; wiki tutorial targets combine 3.

tutorial-book.comment: GitHub wiki 'Quickstart Tutorial' plus explainer pages, but the tutorial is labelled for combine 3 and has not been updated for 4.x.

notable-users.comment: Both verified via Cargo.toml (redis 4.6.8, graphql-parser 4.6.6). README also lists toml_edit and tantivy, but toml_edit has since moved to winnow and tantivy's query-grammar now depends on nom 7; mentat is archived.

bus-factor.comment: Markus Westerlind (Marwes) is the sole owner/publisher and merges all PRs; ~55 contributors overall, recent commits are one-off community fixes.
